notes: Arrival at dusk, the bounty board in two states, and the last room at the Sleeping Ox (bible 4.1 beats 1 to 2). Class-specific arrival text is mw-e39.17 and is not here. The board's text is shown when the player reads the notice board on Market Green.

sequences.title: Dusk on the mountain road
sequences.notes: Shown as the player crosses the Miners' Bridge and the main quest starts (briar-glen.arrived).

pages.text: The mountain road comes down out of the pines at the hour when the light goes gold. Below you lies Briar Glen: chimney smoke, a river the colour of tea, and the mine's headframe standing over the roofs like a held breath.
A small crowd has gathered on the Market Green beyond the Miners' Bridge. Someone is nailing a notice to the board, and nobody is looking at the hammer. They are looking at the hill.

sequences.title: The notice board
sequences.notes: Read at the board on the evening of arrival: the first version of the bounty.

pages.text:
WANTED
the BEAST of the DEEPWORKS
Five hundred crowns on proof of its death.
Apply at Vane House.
(signed) H. Vane, Deepworks
Beneath it, older notices curl in the damp: a lost dog, a lantern for sale, and six names in a careful hand, with a line below. Anyone who has seen anything, tell the Watch.

sequences.title: The notice board
sequences.notes: The same board after Vane's speech on the morning after the first night: five hundred raised to eight hundred.

pages.text:
WANTED
the BEAST of the DEEPWORKS
Eight hundred crowns on proof of its death.
The child Tansy Pell has been taken. Apply at Vane House.
(signed) H. Vane, Deepworks

sequences.title: The last room
sequences.notes: Hands off to the first night when the player goes after Tansy; the player can also stay in bed (the day-two timer ends the beat).

pages.text: The Sleeping Ox has one room left, under the eaves, over the kitchen. Dot Farrow hands you the key and a candle and does not ask your business. She has asked everyone else's already.
The town goes to bed early now, and carefully, as if quiet were a shutter that could be latched. A little after midnight even the dogs have stopped.
You wake and cannot say why. The street is silent. Then, under the window, something that is not the wind: someone humming, slow and sweet and a little flat.

It is a girl of twelve, barefoot, in a nightgown, her eyes open and seeing nothing. Dot pointed her out at supper: the baker's daughter, Tansy, who reads what she is not supposed to. She is walking up the street, toward the mine.
